# Spec: 007-onboarding-de-orgs
<!-- Generated by /speckit.specify -->
<!-- Date: 2026-09-22 -->

## Overview

The ergonomics of running more than one lab: a guided path for creating an organization, the
co-branding that makes a second lab look like itself rather than like CITe, and the storage quota
the schema has promised since feature 000 and nothing has ever enforced.

**This is ergonomics, not capability, and the named source says so.** `tech-stack.md` §
Multi-tenancy closes its Painéis bullet with *"o requisito fica atendido **em substância desde a
fundação**; o que se adia é a **ergonomia** (wizard de org, tema, quotas)"*. A master can already
create an organization today — through `/admin`, field by field, remembering unaided that the slug
can never be changed. Nothing in this feature makes the platform able to do something it could not
do; it makes the thing it can already do survivable by a human being doing it for the second time.

## The trigger, and what this feature does with it

`sdd-strategy.md` row 007 is the only row carrying a gate: **"gatilho: convênio assinado + 2º lab
real"**. Neither has happened. The PO's decision (2026-09-22) is to build the **application half
now** — so the day a convênio is signed the onboarding is a form rather than a project — and to
leave **TLS multi-host out**, because it is deployment infrastructure with no target in this
repository and a spec written against an imaginary deploy is a spec nobody can verify.

### Multi-host TLS is now owned by nobody, and that is recorded here on purpose

This must be said plainly, because the identical failure has already happened once in this project
and 008 exists to undo it.

`infra/docker-compose.yml`'s header deferred production hardening — TLS, certificates, backups,
monitoring — to "feature 007". 007 was trigger-gated on an event that may never occur, so
**everything needed to put the product on the internet was parked behind a second lab that does not
exist**. `008-implantacao` was written (2026-09-06) to take it back, and its own preamble says so.

008's Scope then reads: *"**Out**: multi-host TLS and per-organization co-branding, which is
genuinely 007's and genuinely gated on a second lab."* Half of that hand-off lands: per-organization
co-branding **is** this feature's, and this feature takes it. The other half does not: with the PO
putting multi-host TLS out of 007 as well, it is out of both and **owned by nothing**.

So this spec records where it goes instead of letting it go missing:

- The mechanism is already decided, not open. `tech-stack.md` § Multi-tenancy: *"TLS:
  `on_demand_tls` do Caddy (HTTP-01 por subdomínio, sem imagem custom nem chave de DNS); wildcard
  DNS-01 apenas como otimização futura."*
- Caddy is **008's** component — 008's FR-001 through FR-003 build the production stack around it.
- Therefore multi-host TLS is a **Caddy configuration change inside 008**, not a feature of its
  own, and the thing it waits on is a second hostname to issue a certificate for.

**What would have to be true to close it:** 008 implemented, a second organization with a real
domain, and DNS pointing at the host. None of those is code this feature could write.

## Scope

**In**: the organization wizard, from slug validation through the first org admin, creating through
the sanctioned path so the seeds fire; co-branding beyond the accent colour — logo and hero art as
real uploads, rendered, with the anonymous-door decision that implies; the per-organization storage
quota, enforced at the one choke point every upload passes through, and `storageUsedMb` made into a
number that is maintained rather than promised; and the deletion of a test exemption that currently
excuses a column on the strength of a job nobody wrote.

**Out**: multi-host TLS (above — it belongs to 008's Caddy configuration); the public maker profile,
which 006's CLR-007 deferred and FR-035 asserts stays unlinked; billing, which the constitution
lists among the v1 exclusions and a quota is not the first half of.

**Deliberately out, with the reason**: a self-serve organization signup. The constitution's LGPD
constraint is unambiguous — *"No external tenant before a signed legal instrument (controller/
operator, DPO, incident notification, explicit no-SLA policy)"* — so a path that lets a stranger
create an organization without a human countersigning would contradict a governing principle. The
wizard is a tool for a master who has already signed something, and that is the whole of its
audience.

## Inherited constraints, each measured on the tree at 38e4369

1. **`organizations` is `masterOnly()` on all four verbs**, and `admin.hidden` refuses any user
   whose role is not master (`collections/Organizations.ts`). **An organization admin cannot read
   their own organization record, let alone edit it.** Every co-branding requirement below inherits
   that, and US4 is where the feature pays for it.

2. **The slug is immutable, enforced rather than advised.** `Organizations.ts`'s `beforeChange`
   throws an `APIError` on any attempted change, because storage keys (`org/<slug>/…`,
   `lib/uploads/keys.ts`) and hostnames derive from it — `admin.readOnly` would only hide the input
   while REST still accepted it. The wizard has exactly one chance to get it right.

3. **`seedNewOrganization` then `revalidateTenantResolution` fire on `afterChange`, in that order**,
   and `SEED_ON_CREATE` holds one entry today: `seedRegrasXp`. An organization created outside that
   path has no XP economy — which is the exact state that made 006's NÍVEL DO LAB card render its
   error state on the developer database (measured 2026-09-21, recorded in
   `fablab-dev-environment`).

4. **`clientUploads: false`** (`payload.config.ts`), decision D1 of feature 002: every upload passes
   through Node. This is what makes a quota enforceable at one place instead of two.

5. **`upload.limits.fileSize` is a single global ceiling** at the largest declared cap, so an image
   is bounded at the *document* cap. `tests/uploads/presign-limit.test.ts` records this as the open
   T016b gap and asserts the two numbers stay unequal so nobody reads it as closed. This feature
   does not inherit it as "size is handled".

6. **The gate set grows and never shrinks** (Principle 5). A quota is a refusal, so it ships with a
   test that watches it refuse.

## Two places the written architecture has gone stale, and what this feature owes them

The constitution's preamble settles precedence: *"when this file and a decision record disagree, the
dated decision record wins and this file is amended."* Both items below are that case, and naming
them is part of this feature's work rather than an aside.

### The quota's stated mechanism describes an architecture the app no longer has

Constitution § Architecture Constraints: *"organization quota is validated **when the presigned URL
is issued**, with a periodic reconciliation job against the bucket prefix."* `tech-stack.md` §
Multi-tenancy says the same thing.

**The app issues no presigned URLs.** Feature 002's D1 set `clientUploads: false` and routes every
upload through Node. So the sentence names an issuance point that does not occur, and a requirement
written from it would enforce a quota on a path no byte travels. The enforcement point that exists
is `refuseOffPolicyUpload` in `collections/Media.ts` — a `beforeOperation` hook that already refuses
on extension and per-group size, and which sees `req.file`.

This feature enforces at the hook and **owes the constitution an amendment** saying so.

### The prescribed reconciliation job has no home, and its own reason argues against the alternative

`tech-stack.md` prescribes *"job periódico de reconciliação contra o prefixo"* and gives the reason
in four words: *"contador denormalizado sofre drift"*.

That reason is real and it is inconvenient, because the machinery this codebase actually has is a
denormalized counter. `lib/content/counters.ts`'s `syncCounter` maintains four derived values inside
the writing transaction, and `tests/content/counters.test.ts` reconciles the whole database against
their sources on every run. **There is no job runner anywhere in this repository** — `scripts/` holds
seven files and all seven are CI gates.

So the choice is between a mechanism the source prescribes and cannot host, and a mechanism the
codebase has and the source warns about. The distinction that resolves it is *what the two
reconcile against*: `counters.test.ts` reconciles against the **database**, while the drift
`tech-stack.md` fears is against the **bucket** — and the bucket is what gets billed. Both are
needed eventually; only one is buildable now. See CLR-003.

## User Scenarios

### US1: A master onboards a second lab without knowing the schema [P1]

- **Given** a signed convênio and a master account
- **When** they open the organization wizard and complete it
- **Then** an organization exists with its name, slug, at least one domain, an LGPD contact, a
  storage quota and a first administrator — and its XP economy was seeded, so the new lab's
  gamified surfaces work on the first request rather than showing error cards

### US2: The slug is refused before it becomes permanent [P1]

- **Given** a master at the wizard's first step
- **When** they enter a slug that is already taken, or is not a valid hostname label
- **Then** the wizard refuses before anything is created, names what is wrong with the value they
  typed, and shows the host and storage prefix the slug would produce
- **Edge case**: a slug that differs from an existing one only by case or by surrounding whitespace
  is a collision, not a new organization
- **Error case**: a collision discovered at creation time rather than at validation time still
  leaves no organization behind

### US3: A second lab looks like itself [P1]

- **Given** an organization with a logo, a hero image and an accent colour
- **When** an anonymous visitor loads its Home
- **Then** the header shows that lab's logo, the hero shows that lab's art, and the accent colour is
  that lab's — none of them CITe's
- **Edge case**: an organization with no logo renders the platform default and the page is whole
- **Error case**: an organization record that cannot be read renders platform defaults and reports
  the problem to the log, never a broken page (feature 001's FR-004, unchanged)

### US4: A master changes a lab's look, and nobody else can [P1]

- **Given** a master and an organization that already exists
- **When** they edit that organization's accent colour, logo or hero image
- **Then** the change appears on that organization's pages and on no other organization's
- **Edge case**: clearing an identity value returns that surface to the platform default rather than
  leaving a gap
- **Error case**: an organization admin — of that very organization — attempting to read or write
  the record is refused, because CLR-005 leaves `organizations` `masterOnly()` untouched and this
  feature asserts that rather than assuming it

### US5: A lab cannot fill the disk [P1]

- **Given** an organization whose stored bytes are at its quota
- **When** a maker uploads a file that would exceed it
- **Then** the upload is refused before the bytes are stored, with a message naming the size, the
  remaining allowance and who can raise the limit
- **Edge case**: an upload that exactly reaches the quota is accepted; only exceeding it is refused
- **Error case**: a maker is never shown another organization's usage, and never a raw byte figure
  with no unit

### US6: The used figure is a number somebody can trust [P1]

- **Given** an organization with uploads, deletions and generated derivatives
- **When** anyone reads its `storageUsedMb`
- **Then** it equals the sum the reconciliation gate computes from the rows that feed it, and the
  gate has no exemption excusing it

### US7: Raising the quota takes effect without a deploy [P2]

- **Given** an organization refused at its quota
- **When** a master raises `storageQuotaMb`
- **Then** the next upload succeeds, with no restart and no code change — the same property
  Principle 3 gives the XP economy

### US8: A half-finished wizard leaves nothing behind [P2]

- **Given** a master partway through the wizard
- **When** creation fails at any step
- **Then** no organization, no seeded economy and no administrator membership survive the failure,
  and the master may start again with the same slug

### US9: A new organization is reachable immediately [P2]

- **Given** an organization created seconds ago with a domain
- **When** a visitor requests that host
- **Then** it resolves to the new organization rather than 404ing until a cache expires

### US10: The wizard is not a public door [P1]

- **Given** a visitor who is not a master — anonymous, maker, or an admin of some organization
- **When** they request the wizard route by URL
- **Then** they are refused, and the refusal does not disclose whether the route exists for anyone
  else

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-021 | Every organization has a storage quota, defaulting to **20 GiB (20480 MB)** at creation, so no organization is unbounded by omission (CLR-004) | P1 | US5 |

| FR-024 | The refusal tells the uploader who can raise the limit, because the person refused is usually not the person who can act | P2 | US5 |
| FR-025 | The refusal carries an HTTP status distinguishable from the per-file cap's, so a client can tell "this file is too big" from "this lab is full" | P1 | US5 |
| FR-026 | Enforcement happens at the one path every upload travels, and a test proves no second path bypasses it | P1 | US5 |
| FR-027 | An upload that exactly reaches the quota is accepted; only exceeding it is refused | P2 | US5 |

| FR-030 | Deleting an upload releases its bytes from the organization's used figure | P1 | US6 |
| FR-031 | The reconciliation gate covers `storageUsedMb`, and **the exemption currently excusing it in `tests/content/counters.test.ts` is deleted in the same change** — a stale exemption is how a gate stops being able to fail | P1 | US6 |
| FR-032 | Raising the quota takes effect on the next upload with no restart and no code change | P2 | US7 |
| FR-032b | Lowering the quota below current usage leaves stored data untouched and refuses every upload until usage falls below the quota; the refusal then says the organization is **above** its quota rather than printing a negative allowance (checklist CHK014, CHK015, CHK035) | P2 | US7 |
| FR-033 | The quota column is **non-null with a default**, and a migration backfills the organizations that predate this feature — so "absent" stops being a state any reader has to interpret | P1 | US5 |
| FR-033b | **Zero means no uploads**, deliberately: it is the only way to suspend a lab's intake without deleting anything, and reading it as "unlimited" would make the most restrictive value the most permissive one | P1 | US5 |

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | An organization created through the wizard has a `regrasXp` row | Integration test reading the new organization's economy, so FR-007 cannot pass by writing rows directly |
| SC-002 | A slug colliding case-insensitively with an existing one is refused before creation | Test creating `Bauru` against an existing `bauru` |
| SC-003 | An attempt to change a slug after creation is still refused | Test asserting the existing `beforeChange` throw survives this feature |
| SC-004 | A failed creation leaves zero organizations with that slug | Test forcing a failure mid-creation, then counting rows |
| SC-005 | ~~The wizard route refuses a maker, an org admin and an anonymous visitor~~ **Superseded 2026-09-27** — `Users` declares no `access.admin`, so Payload redirects unauthenticated requests before any view renders (CHK006). **Now:** The wizard refuses a **maker** and an **org admin** with a 404 that discloses nothing; an **anonymous** visitor gets the same redirect to `/admin/login` every `/admin/*` path gives. | Route test per actor, asserting the status and that the body discloses nothing |
| SC-006 | A second organization's Home renders its own logo, hero and accent colour | Page test against two organizations with different identities, asserting no value of one appears on the other |
| SC-007 | An organization with no logo renders the platform default and the page is whole | Page test with the identity values absent |
| SC-008 | The anonymous door returns the identity values and no other column of the organization record | Door test against a record with every field populated, asserting the absent ones are absent |
| SC-009 | An organization admin cannot read even their OWN organization record | Integration test as an org admin, asserting the refusal — so CLR-005's "we did not widen it" is measured rather than assumed |
| SC-010 | Clearing a logo returns the header to the platform default | Page test with the value removed after having been set |
| SC-011 | An upload that would exceed the quota is refused, and nothing was stored | Test asserting both the refusal and the absence of the object |
| SC-011b | A `storageQuotaMb` of zero refuses every upload, including a one-byte one | Boundary test, so FR-033b cannot be read as "unlimited" by a later reader |
| SC-011c | Every organization that predates this feature carries the default quota after migration | Test counting rows with a null quota; the answer is zero |
| SC-012 | The refusal message contains the file size, the remaining allowance and the quota | Assertion on the message text, so FR-023 cannot pass with a bare "recusado" |
| SC-013 | The quota refusal's status differs from the per-file cap's | Test asserting the two statuses are not equal |
| SC-014 | An upload that exactly reaches the quota succeeds | Boundary test at exactly the limit |
| SC-015 | `storageUsedMb` equals the figure recomputed from its sources for every organization | The existing whole-database reconciliation gate, with the exemption removed |
| SC-015b | A raster upload raises the figure by more than its own file size | Integration test on an image with derivatives, so "originals + derivatives" cannot pass while counting originals |
| SC-015c | ~~A quarantined object is not counted~~ **Superseded 2026-09-27** — CHK003. **Now:** *Dropped with FR-029's exclusion.* | Test placing an object under the quarantine prefix and asserting the figure is unchanged |
| SC-016 | `tests/content/counters.test.ts` contains no exemption naming `storageUsedMb` | Test or grep asserting the absence, so the gate cannot be re-excused quietly |
| SC-017 | Deleting an upload lowers the organization's used figure by that file's size | Integration test measuring before and after |
| SC-018 | Raising the quota admits an upload that was refused a moment earlier | Test refusing, raising, retrying — no restart between |
| SC-019 | No second upload path reaches storage without passing the quota check | Tree scan for callers, in the style of 006's "no second caller" scan |
| SC-020 | The Home's LCP stays within budget with the organization's own hero art | The existing CI-only performance gate |
| SC-021 | The island count is unchanged | The existing island-budget test |
| SC-022 | The constitution records the amendment, with its date and source | Markdown assertion, since Principle 5's gate set includes the docs stage |

## Clarifications

### CLR-001 (2026-09-22) — TLS multi-host is out, and 008's Caddy configuration owns it [scope]

**Decision**: out of this feature, per the PO. Recorded as a Caddy configuration change belonging to
008 rather than as a feature of its own, because `tech-stack.md` already decides the mechanism
(`on_demand_tls`, HTTP-01 per subdomain) and 008 already owns Caddy.

**Rationale**: it is deployment infrastructure with no target in this repository. Writing
requirements against an imaginary deploy produces a spec nobody can verify.

**Impact**: the Overview's orphan note; FR-037.

### CLR-002 (2026-09-22) — the wizard is master-only and there is no self-serve signup [security]

**Decision**: the wizard's only audience is a master. No path exists for anyone to create an
organization for themselves.

**Rationale**: the constitution's LGPD constraint — *"No external tenant before a signed legal
instrument"* — makes a self-serve door a contradiction of a governing principle, not a feature
increment.

**Impact**: FR-009, US10, SC-005.

### CLR-003 (2026-09-22) — `storageUsedMb` is a same-transaction derivation; bucket reconciliation is recorded, not built [data lifecycle]

**Decision**: maintain `storageUsedMb` with the machinery this repository has — `syncCounter`'s
derivation inside the writing transaction, covered by the whole-database reconciliation gate — and
delete the exemption that currently excuses it. The bucket-versus-database reconciliation
`tech-stack.md` asks for is **recorded as an open gap**, not built.

**Rationale**: there is no job runner in this repository and `scripts/` holds only CI gates, so the
prescribed periodic job has no home; building a scheduler to host one function is a stack addition
requiring written justification under Principle 1. The drift `tech-stack.md` warns about is real but
is drift against the **bucket**, which is a different question from the one the database gate
answers — and an unenforced quota today is a worse failure than an unreconciled figure tomorrow.

**Impact**: FR-028, FR-031, FR-036, SC-015, SC-016.

### CLR-004 (2026-09-22) — the default quota is 20 GiB [performance]

**Decision**: `storageQuotaMb` defaults to **20480 MB (20 GiB)** for every organization, applied at
creation and backfilled onto the organizations that predate this feature. **Zero means no uploads**
— a suspension state — and after the backfill the column is never absent.

**Rationale**: roughly 200 meshes at the 100 MB per-file cap, or several thousand project photos —
years of a working lab, so nobody meets it by accident in year one. It is also small enough that a
campus VM disk holds it beside Postgres and a second lab, which is the failure `tech-stack.md`
names as number one. Raising it is an edit, not a deploy (FR-032), so the cost of guessing low is
one form field and the cost of guessing high is a full disk.

Zero is read as *no uploads* rather than *unlimited* deliberately: a scheme in which the most
restrictive value a person can type turns out to be the most permissive one is a trap, not a
default.

**Impact**: FR-021, FR-033, FR-033b, SC-011b, SC-011c. Closes `tech-stack.md`'s *"o número da quota
por org ainda não existe — decidir"*.

### CLR-005 (2026-09-22) — co-branding RENDERS for every lab; editing stays master-only [security]

**Decision**: the logo, hero and accent colour are read and rendered per organization, for anonymous
visitors included. **Editing them stays master-only**, and `organizations` keeps `masterOnly()` on
all four verbs — unchanged by this feature.

**Rationale**: the two halves have very different prices. Rendering is read-path work that makes a
second lab look like itself, and it is needed the moment a second lab exists. Editing by an
organization admin requires an access change on **the collection that is the tenant** — the
highest-risk change available in this codebase — and it buys ergonomics for an administrator who
does not exist yet, on the feature whose own trigger has not fired. Feature 006 already added a
sixth named exemption to `lib/tenancy`; a seventh should be bought by a need, not by anticipation.

The negative is asserted rather than assumed: FR-018 and SC-009 measure that an organization admin
still cannot read even their own record, so "we did not widen it" is a test rather than a belief.

**Impact**: US4 rewritten; FR-018, FR-019 rewritten; SC-009, SC-010 rewritten. FR-017 stands — the
anonymous door still widens to serve the identity values the pages render, because that is the
rendering half and it is in scope.

**Deferred, and the trigger for revisiting**: the day a second lab has an administrator who needs to
change their own logo without asking a master.

### CLR-006 (2026-09-22) — `storageUsedMb` counts uploads plus derivatives, never quarantine [data lifecycle]

> **Amended 2026-09-27 (checklist CHK003).** The quarantine half of this
> decision addresses no rows: no live upload is ever written under the
> quarantine prefix, because the only constructor that produces such keys,
> `generateObjectKey`, has no production caller. The exclusion is withdrawn
> with SC-015c. Counting derivatives stands.

**Decision**: the figure sums each upload **and its generated derivatives** (`miniatura`, `card`),
and **excludes the quarantine prefix**.

**Rationale**: the quota exists to stop a lab filling the disk, and the disk holds derivatives — a
figure counting only originals lets a lab sit at "80% of quota" with a full disk, which is the
quota failing at the one job it has. Quarantine is excluded for the opposite reason: it is transient
and reaped, so counting it would refuse one maker's upload because of another's un-reaped garbage,
for a reason nobody could act on.

The known cost is recorded rather than discovered later: the figure **moves if the derivative widths
are ever changed**. That is real, and a test asserting the relationship makes such a move
deliberate instead of a mystery in a reconciliation run.

**Impact**: FR-029, SC-015b, SC-015c.

## Open questions

*None.* The three this spec opened were answered on 2026-09-22 and are recorded as CLR-004, CLR-005
and CLR-006 above.
